page: Amazon Web Services r8g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores with 64 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz via AWS Neoverse-V2 processors. Each core is provisioned with a single thread, eliminating hyperthreading contention. The CPU cache architecture comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by hardware-accelerated AES cryptographic instruction support.

Hardware specifications include 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance provides 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It includes zero discrete GPUs and features no bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal exceptional throughput in memory-bound and heavily multi-threaded workloads. The r8g.16xlarge achieved top-tier rankings in memory bandwidth testing, reaching 463.55 GB/sec on large-block uncached reads and 215.12 GB/sec on large-block writes, alongside 132.23 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Compute benchmarks show balanced single-core execution with Geekbench single-core at 1879.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1706.6, while multi-core performance places in the top decile with a Geekbench multi-core score of 25270.0 and clang compilation at 81224.0. Large language model inference demonstrates stable throughput on 7B and 70B parameter models, though single-threaded text generation on minimal models remains constrained.

The absence of local NVMe storage requires architectural consideration for IOPS latency over network interfaces, but the high memory density delivers substantial resource efficiency for large memory footprints without overpaying for unused acceleration hardware. Amazon Web Services r8g.16xlarge is suited for in-memory databases such as Redis, large relational database operations, distributed caching systems, large-scale code compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive data processing.
